chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Barnet and the clarinet
summary: He seldom played clarinet, disliked it, and used it only for effects.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: The 6th of March, 1943. Okay. You haven't mentioned clarinet at all.
Oh, I very seldom used the clarinet. I did on one record, "Lament For A Lost Love," but not as a -- I didn't play any solos. I played -- they had the traditional

"Mood Indigo" trio there, the muted trombone and trumpet and the sub-tone clarinet. I played that on it, but I never played any solos on clarinet, because to be very frank, I was very awkward on the instrument and I didn't like it, I didn't like to play it, and I didn't play it very well, and I always figured there was other guys around, you know, could do a lot better. I just forgot about it, but once in a while I'd get pressed into service, because maybe Billy or Andy had those guys doing something else and they needed a clarinet for an effect or something like that. That would be the only way I would use the clarinet.
